page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processors using the x86_64 architecture. It features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per physical core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong performance in memory-intensive operations and specific single-threaded tasks. The server achieved strong ratings in large-block memory bandwidth, with read-only speeds of 210.08 GB/sec and write speeds of 98.02 GB/sec. It also demonstrated strong capabilities in software compilation using Clang and single-threaded Gzip compression. However, CPU performance in multi-core stress tests and standard database operations falls in the average range, and LLM text generation speeds are weak to poor, with the 7B model generating only 7.8 tokens per second.

Given its massive memory footprint and high-frequency dedicated Intel processors, this bare-metal instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached options, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is highly suited for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, software compilation pipelines, and high-throughput network applications requiring substantial RAM.
